## Reader content and search decision

The scheduled 2026-08-22 Korean web-novel ecosystem / translated-editions asset shipped through pull request #109. The article `2026 韩国网文怎么找？从韩文原站到英语正式版的完整路线图` contains more than 6,000 Chinese/Han main-text characters before references, 22 academic references and 27 first-party/platform/industry/community sources. Research used multiple Korean- and English-language public-web rounds plus multiple Korean/English Scholar rounds. The 2026 MezzoMedia Web Contents report was inspected from the PDF itself, including the n=1,000 survey context, 18% Web-novel usage signal, and age/platform table.

The article's original synthesis is a three-coordinate work-identity model: origin coordinates establish Korean title/author/origin platform; version coordinates connect serialization, ebook, and adaptation variants; export coordinates connect English titles and first-party publishers. A reusable identity graph then records same-work, version-of, adapted-as, and published-by relationships. The article also separates Korean-platform ranking signals, translation-index visibility, English-platform selection, and community discussion instead of treating them as one popularity metric.

The required author-written-body literal scan found zero matches for the repository's defensive-negation vocabulary, including the listed `不` / `没` / `无` / `未` families and compound patterns. A separate semantic review confirmed affirmative framing, source-role separation, bounded community claims, scoped access/legal claims, and no unsupported negative assertion introduced by paraphrase. The current RIDI citation uses the corrected first-party v4.14 / 2026-04-02 terms evidence.

Search Console evidence remains unavailable, so no speculative title, keyword, canonical, internal-link, routing, CTR, or ranking experiment is justified. `https://www.webnovel.win/` remains the sole documentation/editorial/search identity and `https://app.webnovel.win/` remains the reader runtime. ## Source growth program

### New candidates discovered

Five previously untracked Korean platform families were screened today: 노벨피아 / Novelpia, 브릿G / BritG, OneStory, Bookcube, and MrBlue. This meets the daily minimum of five new source or collection candidates.

### Full audits

**Novelpia — PASS for link-only discovery; richer adapter deferred.** The current first-party platform exposes search, ranking, free-serialization, and PLUS discovery routes. Current service terms took effect on 2026-08-13, and the public service pages preserve site/rightsholder interests in registered content. WebNR therefore stores only the first-party destination plus authored discovery metadata. It does not copy story text, episodes, covers, ranking values, comments, membership/account/payment state, or platform catalog data. Any richer adapter requires an explicitly permitted machine interface and complete versioned runtime fixtures.

**BritG — PASS for link-only discovery; richer adapter deferred.** Current first-party fiction, serial, review, and community surfaces are reachable. Published member and registered-author terms preserve author/member content rights and restrict unauthorized reuse of service-obtained material. WebNR therefore admits the official destination plus authored metadata only; it does not ingest works, episodes, reviews, comments, author/account/purchase information, or platform-owned datasets.

**OneStory — DEFER for richer integration.** ONE store's first-party product material currently identifies OneStory as a Webtoon, Web-novel, and ebook service, and current reader/discovery surfaces are available. This cycle did not establish a sufficiently complete service-specific machine-interface, request-cadence, rights/access, update/deletion, and reproducible-fixture contract for a richer source. It remains deferred rather than inferring automation permission from public discoverability.
